name: typewriter-effect

frames.best_why: The full headline is typed out with the blue final word and blinking cursor visible.

tagline: A bold headline types itself out letter by letter behind a blue caret.
summary: A small grey eyebrow line above a large bold headline that fills in one character at a time when it enters view. A thin blue cursor bar blinks after the text and the last word is blue.
appearance: A black stage with a small grey sentence above a large bold white headline. The headline types out left to right with a thin blue vertical caret after it, and the final word is blue and wraps onto a second line.
behaviour: When it scrolls into view the characters pop in one after another with a stagger, revealing each word. The blue caret blinks continuously and the last word stays blue once printed.
demo_content: The line The road to freedom starts from here and the headline Build awesome apps with Aceternity.
search_phrases: text reveal when scrolled into view
use_when: A short headline or slogan that should feel typed in as the page loads.
avoid_when: Long or essential copy: characters begin hidden, and the caret blinks without pause.
customise: Pass a words array of text plus optional per-word className; the caret colour and size come from cursorClassName and styles, while timing is fixed.
weight_why: Words are split into character spans with one stagger; the caret loop is trivial.

a11y.note: Each letter is its own span, so screen readers may spell the headline out, and reduced-motion is not handled.

issues: The final word wraps mid-animation, jumping the headline to two lines in frames 4 and 5.
Characters start hidden, so nothing is visible until the block scrolls into view.
The blue caret blinks forever with no reduced-motion pause.
polish_why: Crisp type and a tidy stagger; the late wrap makes the headline jump between rows.
title: Typewriter Effect
